title: Adaptive Mosaic: Fingerprint-driven batch policy pipeline and safe rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build an automated recommendation engine that converts continuous workload fingerprints into safe batching and caching parameter proposals and deploys them via a shadow-first rollout. Scope: workload fingerprint extraction (latency/token distribution, seq-length histograms, prefix reuse rates), a heuristics engine that maps fingerprints to parameter vectors (microbatch size, max coalesce window, KV cache TTL, prefix cache policies), and a controlled apply pipeline with shadow-apply, canary, and gated rollback. Non-goals: model architecture changes, lower-level kernel scheduling (left to runtime team), or complex RL-based tuning in this phase. Background: current manual batching tweaks reduce cost but are brittle across workloads (bursty chat vs steady embedder). The engine will synthesize a compact fingerprint, look up heuristics and cost/SLAs models, and propose a delta from baseline. Safety: proposals must pass offline quality and latency regressions, cost delta bounds, and staged rollout checks. Key deliverables: fingerprint service proto, heuristics ruleset with fallback bands, simulator that runs proposals against replayed trace, rollout controller integrating with Console rollouts and the runtime's shadow-apply APIs, and telemetry and alerting hooks for rollback triggers. Risks: output-quality drift (prompt-specific regressions), edge workloads with high prefix reuse that break coalescing assumptions, and interaction with Dedicated autoscaling. Mitigations: conservative default bands, KL/ROUGE-based quality monitors tied to sampled prompts, and mandatory manual flag for workloads marked high-risk.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint extractor produces a stable 12-dim signature for each workload with <2% variance across 1h windows
Heuristics engine suggests parameter vectors with expected cost improvement and estimated latency impact for 90% of sampled workloads
Simulator shows no more than 3% increase in tail latency P95 for proposals that pass cost threshold >5% savings
Shadow-apply flow can be executed end-to-end and observed in Console for a single customer (sandbox), with automatic rollback on fail conditions
Automated alerts trigger when KL divergence on sampled LLM output exceeds configured threshold within 60 minutes of apply

telemetry_queries: SELECT workload_id, percentile_latency(95) FROM requests WHERE ts > now()-interval '1 hour' GROUP BY workload_id;
SELECT workload_id, avg(seq_len), stddev(seq_len) FROM tokens WHERE ts > now()-interval '24 hours' GROUP BY workload_id;
-- KL divergence placeholder: compute between baseline and shadow outputs on sampled prompts
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Offline simulation against 7-day replay traces; require cost >= 5% improvement and P95 <= +3%
Stage 1: Shadow-apply to 1% traffic for 24 hours; monitor latency, errors, and KL on sampled prompts
Stage 2: Canary apply to 10% traffic for 6 hours with stricter alarms (KL threshold lowered by 20%)
Stage 3: Gradual increase to 100% over 48 hours with continuous monitoring and automated guardrail checks
Abort: defined automatic rollback if any key metric crosses threshold or manual stop by owner
rollback_plan: Immediate revert to previous parameter vector via rollout controller
If revert fails, trigger runtime circuit that pins batch configuration to baseline and divert traffic to dedicated pool
Post-mortem and hold on any re-apply until manual triage and QA validation
